neighbours.label: an everyday resource-using activity or appliance (driving, idling, showers, lights, flying, meat) named as a behaviour to cut back in an energy-saving / carbon-footprint context
neighbours.short: eco-footprint everyday activity to cut back
neighbours.notes: Probes: the same activity words in neutral contexts (a drive along the coast, a shower after a game) stay below 0.07; eco sentences with no consumer activity stay below 0.1.
fire: To lower your emissions, avoid idling your car while you wait in the school pickup line.
Save water and energy by taking shorter showers and washing clothes in cold water.
Help the planet: switch off the lights and unplug chargers when you leave the room.
If you want to shrink your carbon footprint, try biking to work instead of driving.
One easy climate tip is to eat less beef and choose plant-based meals a few times a week.
Cutting back on flying is one of the biggest ways a household can reduce its emissions.
To save electricity, run the dishwasher only when full and hang clothes instead of using the dryer.
Conserve fuel by combining errands into one trip rather than driving across town every day.
